why: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest CloudFront edge location and then over the optimized AWS backbone to the bucket, speeding long-distance transfers from global sites. Combined with multipart uploads for the large daily files, it aggregates data directly into one bucket as quickly as possible with minimal operational complexity, since it is just a bucket setting plus a different endpoint.

others.B: Cross-Region Replication adds extra buckets, replication rules and cleanup steps, increasing complexity and delaying arrival in the destination bucket.
others.C: Shipping Snowball Edge devices daily is slow and operationally heavy when the sites already have high-speed internet.
others.D: Staging data on EC2 and EBS with snapshot copies is complex, slow and does not even land the data in S3.

tip: Global sites uploading quickly to one bucket over the internet: think S3 Transfer Acceleration plus multipart upload.

why: Amazon Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that runs standard SQL directly against data in S3, including JSON, with no infrastructure to manage and pay-per-query pricing. It requires no data movement and minimal architecture changes, giving the least operational overhead for simple on-demand queries.

others.A: Redshift requires provisioning a cluster and loading data, which is more overhead than needed for simple ad hoc queries.
others.B: Moving logs into CloudWatch Logs changes the architecture, and Logs Insights uses its own query language rather than querying the existing S3 data.
others.D: Glue plus a transient EMR Spark cluster is far more operational effort than Athena for simple SQL queries.

tip: Ad hoc SQL on data already in S3 with least overhead: Athena.

why: The aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key in an S3 bucket policy allows access only to principals from accounts in the specified AWS Organizations organization. It is a single condition that automatically covers accounts as they join or leave, so it has the least operational overhead.

others.B: Creating OUs per department and using aws:PrincipalOrgPaths adds unnecessary restructuring when the whole organization should have access.
others.C: Monitoring CloudTrail events and manually updating the bucket policy is reactive and operationally heavy.
others.D: Tagging every user and maintaining aws:PrincipalTag conditions requires ongoing manual effort and is error-prone.

tip: Restrict a resource to your whole organization: aws:PrincipalOrgID in the resource policy.

why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 adds a route in the subnet route table so traffic to S3 stays on the AWS private network without an internet gateway or NAT. It provides private connectivity at no additional charge.

others.B: CloudWatch Logs streaming does not give the instance private network access to read objects in S3.
others.C: An instance profile grants IAM permissions but does not provide a network path to S3 without internet access.
others.D: API Gateway is not the mechanism for private S3 connectivity from a VPC and adds unnecessary complexity.

tip: Private access from a VPC to S3 or DynamoDB: gateway endpoint (free).

why: EBS volumes are attached to a single instance in a single AZ, so each server only sees its own uploaded documents. Amazon EFS is a shared, multi-AZ NFS file system that both instances can mount concurrently, so moving existing data to EFS and writing new documents there gives every request a consistent view of all documents.

others.A: Copying data once does not keep the two volumes in sync as new documents are uploaded.
others.B: Sticky routing ties users to one server but documents uploaded to the other server remain invisible, and it hurts availability.
others.D: An ALB cannot fan out a single request to multiple targets and merge the responses.

tip: Multiple instances across AZs needing the same files: use EFS (or S3), not EBS.

why: Moving 70 TB over the network would take a long time and consume significant bandwidth. An AWS Snowball Edge device lets the company copy data locally and ship it to AWS for import into S3, which is the fastest option while using almost no network bandwidth.

others.A: Copying 70 TB with the AWS CLI uses a large amount of network bandwidth and would be slow.
others.C: S3 File Gateway still transfers all data over the internet connection, consuming bandwidth.
others.D: Provisioning Direct Connect takes weeks and still sends all data over the network.

tip: Tens of TB with limited bandwidth or urgency: Snowball Edge.

why: Publishing to an SNS topic that fans out to multiple SQS queues decouples the producer from dozens of consumers, and each consumer application processes messages from its own queue at its own pace. SNS and SQS standard queues scale virtually without limit, absorbing sudden spikes to 100,000 messages per second.

others.A: Kinesis Data Analytics is for analyzing streaming data, not a message store for many consumers to read.
others.B: Having consumers poll DynamoDB is not a decoupled messaging pattern and does not address ingestion bursts.
others.C: A single Kinesis shard supports only about 1,000 records per second for writes, far below the required peak.

tip: One message, many independent consumers: SNS fan-out to SQS queues.

why: Replacing the primary coordinating server with an SQS queue removes a single point of failure and decouples job submission from processing. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 workers that scales on queue depth (such as backlog per instance) matches capacity to the variable workload, maximizing resiliency and scalability.

others.A: Scheduled scaling does not respond to unpredictable, variable workloads.
others.C: CloudTrail is an audit logging service, not a job destination, and keeping the primary server retains a bottleneck.
others.D: EventBridge is not a job queue for workers, and keeping the primary server limits resiliency.

tip: Variable job workloads: SQS queue plus Auto Scaling based on queue backlog.

why: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an SMB share on premises backed by S3, with a local cache that keeps recently accessed files available at low latency, effectively extending storage capacity. An S3 Lifecycle policy then transitions objects older than 7 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, providing automated lifecycle management at lowest cost.

others.A: DataSync copies data but provides no ongoing access path or lifecycle management for the file server.
others.C: FSx for Windows File Server adds storage but has no lifecycle tiering to archival storage.
others.D: Installing an S3 utility on each computer is operationally heavy and loses the SMB file share experience.

tip: Extend on-prem file storage into AWS with local caching: Storage Gateway (S3 File Gateway).

why: An SQS FIFO queue guarantees first-in-first-out ordering within a message group and exactly-once processing. API Gateway can integrate directly with SQS, and Lambda can poll the FIFO queue as an event source, so orders are processed in the order received.

others.A: A standard SNS topic does not guarantee message ordering to subscribers.
others.C: Blocking requests with an authorizer would reject orders and does not provide ordered processing.
others.D: SQS standard queues provide best-effort ordering only, so orders may be processed out of sequence.

tip: Strict ordering requirement: FIFO (SQS FIFO or SNS FIFO).

why: AWS Secrets Manager stores database credentials securely and has built-in automatic rotation for Amazon Aurora and RDS using managed rotation functions. The application retrieves credentials at runtime via API, removing local files and minimizing credential management overhead.

others.B: Systems Manager Parameter Store does not offer native automatic rotation of secrets.
others.C: Storing an encrypted credential file in S3 still requires manual rotation and file management.
others.D: Moving the file to an encrypted EBS volume improves encryption only and still requires manual credential management.

tip: Database credentials with automatic rotation: Secrets Manager.

why: A single CloudFront distribution can have multiple origins: the S3 bucket for static content and the ALB for dynamic content, using cache behaviors with path patterns. CloudFront edge locations cache static content and accelerate dynamic content over the AWS network, and a Route 53 alias record points the custom domain to the distribution.

others.B: Global Accelerator does not support S3 buckets as endpoints.
others.C: Global Accelerator cannot use a CloudFront distribution as an endpoint, and the design is needlessly complex.
others.D: S3 is not a valid Global Accelerator endpoint, and splitting content across two domain names is unnecessary.

tip: Static plus dynamic content acceleration under one domain: one CloudFront distribution with multiple origins.

why: Secrets Manager supports multi-Region secret replication, keeping replica secrets in sync across Regions, and has built-in scheduled rotation for RDS for MySQL. This fully managed approach rotates credentials across Regions with the least operational overhead.

others.B: Using the RDS API directly requires custom scripting per Region and per database and does not manage credential distribution.
others.C: Storing credentials in S3 with custom Lambda rotation requires building and maintaining your own rotation logic.
others.D: Combining KMS multi-Region keys, DynamoDB global tables and Lambda is a custom solution with high overhead.

tip: Cross-Region secrets with rotation: Secrets Manager multi-Region replication.

why: Amazon Aurora MySQL is compatible with MySQL 8.0, and a Multi-AZ Aurora cluster provides high availability with fast failover. Aurora Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes Aurora Replicas (up to 15) based on metrics such as CPU or connections, handling unpredictable read workloads.

others.A: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not an OLTP transactional database, and a single node lacks high availability.
others.B: A Single-AZ deployment is not highly available, and RDS does not automatically scale the number of read replicas.
others.D: Memcached on Spot Instances is not a durable transactional database and Spot can be interrupted.

tip: Auto-scaling read capacity for a relational DB: Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas.

why: The option text for C is missing in this question bank; the intended answer is AWS Network Firewall. AWS Network Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall with intrusion prevention that inspects and filters traffic flowing in and out of a VPC, replicating the on-premises inspection server's traffic flow inspection and filtering functions.

others.A: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes logs; it does not filter or block traffic inline.
others.B: Traffic Mirroring copies traffic for out-of-band analysis but cannot filter or block traffic.
others.D: Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall policies across accounts but is not itself the inspection engine; it relies on services like Network Firewall.

tip: Inline VPC traffic inspection and filtering: AWS Network Firewall. Option C text is blank here; it should read 'Use AWS Network Firewall'.

why: Amazon QuickSight can connect to both S3 (via Athena or a manifest) and RDS for PostgreSQL to build datasets, analyses and dashboards. QuickSight dashboards are shared with QuickSight users and groups, letting the management team have full access while others get limited permissions.

others.A: QuickSight dashboards are shared with QuickSight users and groups, not directly with IAM roles.
others.C: Glue ETL reports in S3 do not provide interactive data visualization and ignore the RDS data source.
others.D: Athena-generated reports in S3 are not a visualization solution, and bucket policies give coarse access control.

tip: BI dashboards with per-user access: QuickSight shared with users and groups.

why: An IAM role attached to EC2 through an instance profile provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials to applications on the instances. Granting S3 bucket permissions in the role's policy is the AWS best practice for letting EC2 access S3 without storing long-term keys.

others.B: An IAM policy cannot be attached directly to an EC2 instance; it must be attached to a role used via an instance profile.
others.C: IAM groups contain users only and cannot be attached to EC2 instances.
others.D: IAM users cannot be attached to instances, and embedding user access keys is a security anti-pattern.

tip: AWS service needs permissions: use an IAM role, never stored access keys.

why: Configuring S3 event notifications to send a message to an SQS queue durably records every upload, and configuring the Lambda function with the SQS queue as its event source processes each image statelessly. Lambda deletes messages after successful processing, and failed messages become visible again for retry, giving a durable, stateless, automatic pipeline.

others.C: Tracking processed files in an in-memory text file is stateful and is lost when the Lambda execution environment is recycled.
others.D: An EC2 instance logging file names to a local file is stateful, not durable, and adds servers to manage.
others.E: Emailing the application owner via SNS introduces manual processing rather than automatic compression.

tip: S3 upload to async processing durably: S3 event to SQS to Lambda.

why: Gateway Load Balancer is designed to deploy, scale and manage third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls, using GENEVE encapsulation to pass IP packets transparently. Deploying the GWLB in the inspection VPC in front of the appliance, with Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in the application VPC route tables, inspects all traffic before it reaches the web servers with the least operational overhead.

others.A: A Network Load Balancer cannot transparently insert an inline inspection appliance into the traffic path.
others.B: An Application Load Balancer works at layer 7 and cannot forward raw IP packets to an appliance for inspection.
others.C: A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint alone is not enough; it must connect to a Gateway Load Balancer that fronts the appliance.

tip: Third-party virtual appliances inline (firewall, IDS/IPS): Gateway Load Balancer.

why: Volumes restored from snapshots normally load blocks lazily from S3, causing high first-access latency. EBS fast snapshot restore creates volumes that are fully initialized at creation, delivering full provisioned performance immediately, so test environments get independent, high-I/O copies with minimal clone time.

others.A: Instance store volumes are ephemeral and cannot be restored directly from EBS snapshots.
others.B: Multi-Attach shares the production volumes themselves, so test modifications would affect production, and it is limited to io1/io2.
others.C: You cannot restore a snapshot into an already-created volume, and manually initializing volumes is slow.

tip: Snapshot-restored volume needs full performance immediately: EBS fast snapshot restore.

why: The keyed answer uses EC2 Auto Scaling groups across multiple AZs behind ALBs with RDS for MySQL, which can scale to millions of requests per hour while remaining highly available. However, this design carries significant operational overhead from managing instances, AMIs, patching and database scaling.

others.A: S3 alone cannot run backend order processing logic, and storing order data as S3 objects is not suitable for transactional data.
others.C: Running EKS with the Cluster Autoscaler and RDS adds substantial operational overhead for cluster and node management.
others.D: S3 with CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB is fully serverless, scales automatically to millions of requests with millisecond latency, and has the least operational overhead.

tip: LEAST operational overhead plus spiky massive traffic usually points to serverless: S3/CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB.
flag: The keyed answer B is likely wrong; D (S3 + CloudFront + API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) is serverless and meets the LEAST operational overhead requirement, and is the widely accepted answer.

why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on actual access patterns, with no retrieval fees, making it ideal for mixed and unpredictable access. It stores data across multiple AZs, so it is resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone while minimizing storage and retrieval costs.

others.A: S3 Standard charges the higher frequent-access price for rarely accessed files.
others.C: S3 Standard-IA charges retrieval fees, which become costly for frequently accessed files.
others.D: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and is not resilient to AZ loss.

tip: Unknown or changing access patterns: S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

why: The keyed answer transitions objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-IA after 1 month via a Lifecycle rule, which lowers storage cost while keeping millisecond access. However, because the files are never accessed again and must be kept indefinitely, a colder archival class is much cheaper.

others.A: Intelligent-Tiering adds a per-object monitoring fee and is meant for unpredictable access, while this pattern is known.
others.B: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class for data that is never accessed but retained indefinitely, so this is the most cost-effective choice.
others.D: One Zone-IA is cheaper than Standard-IA but stores backups in a single AZ and is still far costlier than Deep Archive.

tip: Known pattern, never accessed after N days, keep forever: Lifecycle to Glacier Deep Archive.
flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; B (Lifecycle transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month) is the most cost-effective for files never accessed again and kept indefinitely.

why: The keyed answer exports AWS Cost and Usage Reports to S3 and visualizes them in QuickSight, which provides the most detailed line-item data for building interactive graphs by instance type. However, it requires setting up CUR delivery, datasets and dashboards, which is more overhead than necessary.

others.A: AWS Budgets is for tracking spend against thresholds and alerting, not for in-depth historical root cause analysis.
others.B: Cost Explorer natively graphs up to 12+ months of cost and supports granular filtering and grouping by instance type with no setup, giving the least operational overhead.
others.C: The Billing dashboard graphs are high-level and lack granular filtering by instance type.

tip: Quick graphing and filtering of recent costs: Cost Explorer.
flag: The keyed answer D is likely wrong; B (Cost Explorer granular filtering by instance type) meets the LEAST operational overhead requirement without building a CUR and QuickSight pipeline.

why: The keyed answer splits the work into a receiving Lambda function and a loading Lambda function connected by SNS, decoupling ingestion from database writes. However, SNS pushes each message immediately to the subscriber, so it does not buffer load or let the loader control its concurrency against Aurora.

others.A: Refactoring to Tomcat on EC2 increases configuration and management effort and does not inherently improve scalability.
others.B: Migrating from Aurora PostgreSQL to DynamoDB with DAX is a major platform change and DAX only accelerates reads.
others.D: An SQS queue between two Lambda functions durably buffers spikes and lets the loader consume in batches at a controlled rate, improving scalability with minimal configuration.

tip: Buffer bursts in front of a database: SQS queue, not SNS.
flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; D (two Lambda functions decoupled by an SQS queue) is the accepted answer because SQS buffers and throttles load to the database.

why: The keyed answer uses AWS Trusted Advisor, whose S3 bucket permissions check flags buckets with open access. However, Trusted Advisor only runs periodic best-practice checks and does not track or evaluate configuration changes over time.

others.A: AWS Config records S3 bucket configuration history and evaluates changes against managed rules such as s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, which directly detects unauthorized configuration changes.
others.C: Amazon Inspector scans EC2, ECR images and Lambda for vulnerabilities, not S3 bucket configurations.
others.D: S3 server access logging records object requests, not bucket configuration changes, and requires custom processing.

tip: Track and audit resource configuration changes: AWS Config.
flag: The keyed answer B is likely wrong; A (AWS Config with appropriate rules) is the service built to detect unauthorized configuration changes.

why: The keyed answer creates an IAM user with the ViewOnlyAccess managed policy and shares credentials with the product manager. However, it is described as an IAM user for the company's employees (shared credentials) and ViewOnlyAccess grants view access far beyond one dashboard, violating least privilege.

others.A: CloudWatch dashboard sharing lets you share a dashboard with specific email addresses so people without an AWS account can view only that dashboard, which best fits least privilege.
others.B: A dedicated IAM user with CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess grants read access to all CloudWatch data, more than just the dashboard.
others.D: A bastion server with cached credentials is complex, insecure and not least privilege.

tip: Someone without an AWS account needs to view a CloudWatch dashboard: share the dashboard by email.
flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; A (share the CloudWatch dashboard with the product manager's email) is the least-privilege answer for a user with no AWS account.

why: AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO) integrates with AWS Organizations to provide single sign-on to all accounts. By deploying AWS Managed Microsoft AD and creating a trust with the self-managed on-premises AD, users and groups continue to be managed on premises while Identity Center uses them for access.

others.B: The keyed answer reflects the bank's view that a one-way trust suffices; note that AWS documentation actually requires a two-way trust between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and on-premises AD for IAM Identity Center.
others.C: Directory Service with a trust alone does not provide SSO across all Organization accounts.
others.D: Deploying an on-premises IdP is extra infrastructure, and the option does not describe connecting it to IAM Identity Center.

tip: SSO across Organizations accounts with existing AD: IAM Identity Center plus AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust.
flag: AWS documentation states IAM Identity Center requires a two-way trust between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and the self-managed AD, so B is arguably correct rather than A.

why: The keyed answer uses NLBs, which support UDP, with Route 53 latency-based records pointing to each Regional NLB, routing users to the lowest-latency Region; health checks on the alias records can provide failover. However, DNS-based failover is subject to client caching and TTLs.

others.A: AWS Global Accelerator supports UDP, routes users over the AWS backbone to the lowest-latency healthy NLB endpoint, and fails over between Regions in seconds without DNS caching issues, making it the best fit.
others.B: CloudFront does not support UDP traffic and cannot use a Route 53 record as an origin in this way.
others.D: ALBs only support HTTP/HTTPS and cannot handle UDP, and weighted routing does not select by latency.

tip: UDP, multi-Region, lowest latency, fast failover: Global Accelerator with NLB endpoints.
flag: The keyed answer C is likely wrong; A (NLBs as AWS Global Accelerator endpoints) is the accepted answer for UDP with lowest latency and automated multi-Region failover.

why: Because the database is only used for 48 hours a month, taking a snapshot and deleting the instance means paying only for snapshot storage for the rest of the month. Restoring the snapshot to the same instance class when needed preserves the compute and memory attributes, making this the most cost-effective option.

others.A: A stopped RDS instance still incurs storage charges and automatically restarts after 7 days, so it would run for much of the month.
others.B: RDS does not support Auto Scaling of DB instance compute size.
others.D: Downsizing still incurs ongoing instance charges and repeated modifications cause downtime and effort.

tip: RDS stopped instances auto-start after 7 days; for rare long gaps, snapshot and delete.

why: AWS Config has a managed rule, required-tags, that continuously evaluates supported resources such as EC2 instances, RDS DB instances and Redshift clusters and flags those missing required tags. It is a managed check that requires minimal effort to configure and operate.

others.B: Cost Explorer can filter by tags but does not continuously detect noncompliant resources, and manual tagging is effortful.
others.C: Custom API scripts on an EC2 instance require building and maintaining code and infrastructure.
others.D: A scheduled Lambda with custom API calls still requires writing and maintaining code.

tip: Continuous compliance checks for tags or settings: AWS Config rules.

why: The site is purely static content (HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript and images), which S3 static website hosting serves directly. You pay only for storage and requests, with no servers to run, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Fargate containers incur continuous compute charges and are unnecessary for static files.
others.C: An EC2 web server incurs ongoing instance costs and management overhead.
others.D: An ALB with Lambda incurs hourly ALB charges and is designed for dynamic content.

tip: Static website with no server-side code: S3 static website hosting (optionally behind CloudFront).

why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests millions of transactions in near real time and allows multiple internal applications to consume the same stream concurrently. A Lambda consumer removes sensitive data from each record and writes the sanitized transactions to DynamoDB, a document database with low-latency retrieval.

others.A: Storing raw transactions directly in DynamoDB does not remove sensitive data first or provide a sharing mechanism for other applications.
others.B: Consuming transaction files from S3 is batch-oriented, not near real time, and does not address data sanitization.
others.D: Batching files in S3 introduces delay and is not a near-real-time streaming design.

tip: Near-real-time stream shared by multiple consumers: Kinesis Data Streams.

why: AWS Config records resource configurations and keeps a history of configuration changes for compliance and auditing. AWS CloudTrail records API calls made in the account, including who made them, when and from where, so together they meet both requirements.

others.A: This reverses the roles; CloudTrail records API calls while Config tracks configuration changes.
others.C: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs; it does not natively record a history of API calls.
others.D: CloudTrail does not provide configuration history, and CloudWatch does not record API call history.

tip: Config = what changed in resource configuration; CloudTrail = who called which API.

why: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced detection and mitigation of large-scale DDoS attacks for protected resources such as Elastic Load Balancers, plus 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team and DDoS cost protection. Because DNS is hosted by a third party, protecting the ELB itself is the correct choice.

others.A: GuardDuty detects threats from logs but does not mitigate DDoS attacks.
others.B: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, not DDoS attacks.
others.C: Route 53 is not used because DNS is with a third party, and Shield Standard lacks the advanced large-scale DDoS detection and response.

tip: Large-scale DDoS protection with response team and cost protection: Shield Advanced on ELB, CloudFront, Global Accelerator, Route 53 or EIPs.

why: A customer managed multi-Region KMS key creates related keys in each Region that share the same key material and key ID, so data can be encrypted in one Region and decrypted in another with the same key, and the key exists in both Regions. With S3 replication between buckets, client-side encryption with that key ensures consistent encryption using one logical key.

others.A: SSE-S3 uses S3 managed keys, not a customer managed KMS key.
others.C: SSE-S3 does not use the customer managed KMS keys, and separate keys per Region are not the same key.
others.D: Separate single-Region KMS keys in each Region are different keys, violating the same-key requirement.

tip: Same KMS key usable in multiple Regions: multi-Region keys.

why: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure, auditable shell access to EC2 instances through the SSM Agent and an IAM instance role, with no open inbound ports, bastion hosts or SSH keys to manage. It is a native, repeatable approach aligned with the Well-Architected Framework and has the least operational overhead.

others.A: The EC2 serial console is intended for troubleshooting boot and network issues, not routine administration at scale.
others.C: Managing SSH keys and a bastion host adds operational overhead and attack surface.
others.D: A Site-to-Site VPN with SSH keys adds infrastructure and key management overhead.

tip: Secure remote instance access without SSH keys or bastions: Session Manager.

why: Amazon CloudFront caches the static website content at edge locations worldwide, reducing latency for global users, and Route 53 alias records can point the domain to the distribution. It is inexpensive and often reduces S3 data transfer costs, making it the most cost-effective option.

others.A: Replicating the bucket to all Regions multiplies storage and replication costs and adds complexity.
others.B: Global Accelerator does not support S3 buckets as endpoints and is more expensive.
others.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to S3, not content delivery to website viewers.

tip: Reduce global latency for static content: CloudFront.

why: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) storage delivers consistent, high, provisioned I/O performance with low latency, which suits I/O-intensive workloads with millions of daily writes. Since storage performance is the bottleneck, moving from General Purpose SSD to Provisioned IOPS directly addresses the slow inserts.

others.B: A memory optimized instance class addresses memory limits, not storage I/O performance.
others.C: A burstable instance class reduces sustained compute and does not improve storage I/O.
others.D: Read replicas offload reads but do not speed up insert operations on the primary.

tip: RDS storage I/O bottleneck: switch to Provisioned IOPS SSD.

why: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, highly available service that ingests streaming data and delivers it to S3 without infrastructure to manage. Storing alerts in S3 keeps 14 days available for analysis, and an S3 Lifecycle rule transitions older data to S3 Glacier automatically, making this the most operationally efficient and low-cost option.

others.B: EC2 instances behind an ELB with custom scripts add infrastructure to manage and higher cost.
others.C: An OpenSearch cluster is more expensive and requires managing snapshots and data deletion.
others.D: SQS is not a storage or analytics platform, and custom consumers checking message age add complexity.

tip: Managed streaming ingestion to S3: Kinesis Data Firehose, then Lifecycle rules for archiving.

why: Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed integration service that securely transfers data from SaaS applications to S3 without custom code or EC2 instances, removing the performance bottleneck. An S3 event notification to an SNS topic handles the upload-complete notification, giving the best performance with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Scaling EC2 instances still requires managing servers and custom ingestion code.
others.C: EventBridge rules per SaaS source cannot write data directly to S3 as a target, and this requires more configuration.
others.D: Containerizing on ECS still requires managing the ingestion code, and Container Insights does not emit S3 upload events.

tip: SaaS to AWS data transfer without code: Amazon AppFlow.

why: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 routes S3 traffic privately from the VPC without going through the NAT gateway. Gateway endpoints have no hourly or data processing charges, eliminating NAT gateway data processing costs, making it the most cost-effective choice.

others.A: A NAT gateway per AZ adds hourly charges and still incurs data processing charges for S3 traffic.
others.B: A NAT instance adds management overhead and still routes S3 traffic through a NAT path.
others.D: Dedicated Hosts increase cost and do not affect data transfer charges.

tip: S3 or DynamoDB traffic through NAT is costly: add a free gateway endpoint.

why: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection from on premises to AWS that does not consume the internet link. Routing backup traffic over Direct Connect gives consistent, timely backups to S3 as a long-term solution while freeing internet bandwidth for internal users.

others.A: A VPN still runs over the existing internet connection, so it does not relieve bandwidth, and gateway endpoints are not reachable from on premises this way.
others.C: Ordering Snowball devices daily is operationally heavy and too slow for time-sensitive data.
others.D: S3 service limits are not the cause of the internet bandwidth problem.

tip: Long-term, consistent bandwidth to AWS separate from internet: Direct Connect.

why: S3 Versioning keeps prior versions of objects, so an accidental delete only adds a delete marker and the data can be recovered. MFA Delete requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete object versions or change versioning state, adding a further safeguard against accidental deletion.

others.C: A bucket policy can restrict deletes but does not provide recovery if data is deleted by an authorized user.
others.D: Default encryption protects confidentiality, not against deletion.
others.E: Lifecycle policies manage transitions and expirations and could actually delete data.

tip: Protect from accidental deletion: Versioning plus MFA Delete (or Object Lock).

why: Subscribing an SQS queue to the SNS topic durably stores each notification, and having the Lambda function read from the queue means messages that fail processing become visible again and are retried automatically. This SNS to SQS to Lambda pattern ensures every delivery is eventually ingested without manual reruns.

others.A: Lambda already runs across multiple AZs automatically, and this does not address lost messages.
others.C: More CPU and memory do not fix transient network failures or add retries.
others.D: Lambda has no provisioned throughput setting, and provisioned concurrency would not add durability.

tip: Need retry durability for events: put an SQS queue in front of Lambda.

why: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover PII in S3 objects with no custom code. Macie findings can trigger notifications through EventBridge and SNS to alert administrators, giving the least development effort.

others.A: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities, not PII in S3 objects, and Lifecycle policies cannot be triggered per finding.
others.C: Writing custom PII scanning algorithms in Lambda requires significant development effort.
others.D: Custom scanning in Lambda requires significant development, and Lifecycle policies cannot be triggered on demand per object.

tip: Detect PII or sensitive data in S3: Amazon Macie.

why: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration, with no long-term commitment, and can be cancelled after the event. Creating reservations in each of the three required AZs guarantees capacity for the one-week event.

others.A: Reserved Instances require 1- or 3-year terms, and Regional RIs do not reserve capacity.
others.B: Capacity Reservations are AZ-specific; specifying only the Region does not guarantee capacity in the needed AZs.
others.C: Zonal Reserved Instances do reserve capacity, but they require a 1- or 3-year commitment, which is wasteful for a 1-week event.

tip: Short-term guaranteed capacity in specific AZs: On-Demand Capacity Reservations.

why: Instance store is ephemeral and data is lost if the instance stops or fails. Amazon EFS is a durable, highly available file system that stores data redundantly across multiple AZs and can be mounted by multiple instances, meeting both requirements.

others.A: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not a primary durable store for the catalog.
others.B: A larger instance store is still ephemeral and tied to a single instance.
others.C: Glacier Deep Archive has retrieval times of hours, unsuitable for a live website catalog.

tip: Instance store = ephemeral; for durable shared files, use EFS.

why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering optimizes cost for randomly accessed files in the first year while keeping millisecond access, and Athena can query data in S3 directly. A Lifecycle rule moves files older than 1 year to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, a cheaper class where the acceptable retrieval delay applies, and S3 Glacier Select can query archived data.

others.A: Keeping all files in Glacier Instant Retrieval is costly for randomly accessed recent files due to retrieval fees, and S3 tags cannot be queried for search.
others.C: Glacier Instant Retrieval is pricier than Flexible Retrieval for old files where delay is acceptable, and searching metadata in S3 is cumbersome.
others.D: Running an RDS database for search metadata adds cost and management overhead.

tip: Delay acceptable for old data: move to a colder Glacier tier with Lifecycle.

why: Systems Manager Run Command executes a custom script across many managed instances at once with configurable concurrency and targeting by tags, so a third-party software patch can be applied to all 1,000 instances immediately. This is the fastest way to remediate the critical vulnerability.

others.A: Lambda cannot directly run commands on EC2 instances without additional tooling and custom code.
others.B: Patch Manager is focused on OS and supported package patches with baselines and may not handle this third-party software patch as quickly.
others.C: A maintenance window schedules work for later rather than applying the patch as quickly as possible.

tip: Run an ad hoc script on a fleet now: Systems Manager Run Command.

why: An EventBridge scheduled rule can invoke a Lambda function every morning to query the REST API for the shipping statistics. Amazon SES can send formatted HTML email to multiple recipients, so Lambda builds the HTML report and sends it through SES.

others.A: Kinesis Data Firehose is for streaming delivery, not generating scheduled email reports.
others.C: AWS Glue is an ETL service and is heavier than needed to call a REST API.
others.E: SNS email notifications are plain text and not suitable for formatted HTML reports.

tip: Scheduled job: EventBridge schedule plus Lambda; formatted email: SES, not SNS.

why: Amazon EFS provides a standard POSIX file system that scales automatically to petabytes, is highly available across multiple AZs and is fully managed. EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group can share the EFS file system, meeting scalability, availability and minimal overhead requirements.

others.A: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a standard file system structure.
others.B: EBS volumes are AZ-bound, do not scale automatically, and are not shared across pods in multiple AZs.
others.D: EBS is tied to a single AZ and instance, does not scale automatically, and is not highly available across AZs.

tip: Shared, auto-scaling file system across AZs: EFS.

why: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents any user, including the root user, from deleting or overwriting locked object versions until the retention period expires, satisfying the 10-year non-deletion requirement. A Lifecycle rule keeps records in S3 Standard for immediate access during year 1 and then moves them to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which stores data across multiple AZs for maximum resiliency at the lowest cost.

others.A: Glacier for the full period does not give immediate access in year 1, and access policies can be changed by administrators or root.
others.B: IAM policies can be modified by administrators and do not restrict the root user.
others.D: Governance mode lets users with special permissions bypass retention, and One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing resiliency.

tip: No one, not even root, can delete: Object Lock compliance mode.

why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed native Windows file shares over SMB with Active Directory integration, so users keep accessing files the same way. A Multi-AZ deployment replicates data synchronously across two AZs with automatic failover, giving high availability and durability.

others.A: S3 is object storage and would change how users access files, replacing SMB shares.
others.B: S3 File Gateway is designed for on-premises access to S3, not for replacing Windows file shares on EC2.
others.D: Amazon EFS uses NFS and does not support Windows SMB clients.

tip: Windows SMB file shares in AWS: FSx for Windows File Server (Multi-AZ for HA).

why: Security groups are stateful allow-only firewalls that can reference other security groups as sources. Attaching a security group to the DB instances that allows inbound database traffic only from the security group of the private subnet instances restricts access exactly as required.

others.A: Route tables cannot block traffic within a VPC because the local route always allows communication among subnets.
others.B: Security groups cannot contain deny rules; they only allow traffic.
others.D: VPC peering connects VPCs, not subnets within the same VPC.

tip: Security groups allow only (no deny); reference source security groups for tier-to-tier access.

why: For a Regional API Gateway endpoint with a custom domain name, the ACM certificate must be in the same Region as the API, here ca-central-1. You create the custom domain name, attach the certificate, map it to the API and create a Route 53 alias record to the API Gateway domain, enabling HTTPS with the company's domain.

others.A: Stage variables cannot change the API's default URL or domain.
others.B: For a Regional endpoint the certificate must be in the API's Region, not us-east-1, and no custom domain name is configured.
others.D: us-east-1 certificates are required only for edge-optimized endpoints, and pointing an A record to the company's own domain is circular.

tip: ACM certificate Region: same Region for Regional endpoints and ALB; us-east-1 for CloudFront and edge-optimized APIs.

why: Amazon Rekognition Content Moderation detects inappropriate, unwanted or offensive content in images through a simple API, with no model training. Amazon Augmented AI can route low-confidence predictions to human reviewers, minimizing development effort.

others.A: Amazon Comprehend analyzes text, not images.
others.C: Building and training a custom model in SageMaker requires significant development effort.
others.D: Deploying a custom ML model on Fargate requires building, training and operating the model yourself.

tip: Image or video moderation: Rekognition; text NLP: Comprehend.

why: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers without provisioning, patching or scaling EC2 instances, so the company manages only its applications. ECS services spread tasks across AZs and integrate with Application Auto Scaling for scalability and availability.

others.A: Running Docker on self-managed EC2 instances requires managing the infrastructure.
others.B: ECS on EC2 worker nodes still requires managing the underlying instances.
others.D: Using an ECS-optimized AMI still means managing EC2 instances.

tip: Containers without managing servers: Fargate.

why: Kinesis Data Streams ingests massive volumes of real-time clickstream data from many sources, and Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the data reliably into an S3 data lake. The data can then be loaded into Amazon Redshift for scalable analytics, forming a standard clickstream pipeline at 30 TB per day.

others.A: AWS Data Pipeline is a legacy batch orchestration service and does not handle real-time ingestion from hundreds of sites.
others.B: An Auto Scaling group of EC2 processors requires custom ingestion code and management.
others.C: CloudFront is a content delivery network, not a data ingestion or caching layer for clickstream data.

tip: Clickstream ingestion at scale: Kinesis Data Streams/Firehose to S3, then Redshift or Athena.

why: ALB listeners support redirect actions, so a rule on the HTTP:80 listener can return an HTTP 301 redirect to HTTPS:443. This forwards all requests to HTTPS natively without application changes.

others.A: Network ACLs apply to subnets, not to the ALB itself, and blocking HTTP would drop requests rather than redirect them.
others.B: ALB rules do not rewrite URL text; the correct mechanism is a redirect action.
others.D: An NLB does not perform HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, and SNI is unrelated to redirection.

tip: HTTP to HTTPS redirect: ALB listener rule with redirect action (or CloudFront viewer protocol policy).

why: AWS Secrets Manager stores the database credentials as a secret with built-in automatic rotation for Amazon RDS. Granting the EC2 instance role permission to read the secret lets the application retrieve current credentials at runtime without hardcoding, with the least operational overhead.

others.A: Instance metadata cannot store custom credentials, and custom Lambda rotation adds overhead.
others.B: Managing credentials in an S3 config file with custom Lambda rotation is operationally heavy.
others.D: Parameter Store SecureString parameters do not support native automatic rotation.

tip: Automatic database credential rotation: Secrets Manager.

why: ACM supports importing certificates issued by an external CA, which can then be applied to the ALB listener for TLS termination at the edge. ACM cannot automatically renew imported certificates, but it tracks expiry and emits expiration events and metrics, and the company re-imports the new certificate each year.

others.A: The option text is truncated in this bank, but applying a certificate to the ALB alone does not address importing an externally issued certificate into ACM.
others.B: The option text appears merged in this bank; relying on manual rotation with notifications alone is incomplete without importing the certificate into ACM for the ALB.
others.C: ACM Private CA issues private certificates that public browsers do not trust, and the requirement is an external CA certificate.

tip: External CA certificate on ALB: import into ACM (no auto-renewal for imported certs). Options A and B text appears garbled in this bank.

why: Storing the .pdf files in S3 and using an S3 PUT event notification to invoke a Lambda function to convert each file and write the .jpg back to S3 is fully serverless. S3 scales storage automatically and Lambda scales with demand, charging only per use, making it the most cost-effective scalable design.

others.B: Option B text is missing in this question bank, so it cannot be evaluated.
others.C: EC2 instances with EBS storage in Elastic Beanstalk cost more, and EBS does not scale automatically or share well across instances.
others.D: Elastic Beanstalk with EC2 and EFS incurs constant compute cost and EFS is far more expensive per GB than S3.

tip: Event-driven file conversion: S3 event to Lambda, storing results in S3. Option B text is blank in this bank.

why: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed SMB file shares in AWS for cloud workloads. Amazon FSx File Gateway deployed on premises provides low-latency local caching of the FSx file shares for on-premises users, preserving existing Windows file access patterns over the VPN with minimal overhead.

others.A: Moving everything to FSx without a local cache forces on-premises users to access files over the VPN, increasing latency.
others.B: S3 File Gateway stores files as S3 objects, and cloud workloads would not access the gateway efficiently, changing access patterns.
others.C: Having workloads use S3 directly changes file access patterns from SMB to object APIs.

tip: Hybrid low-latency access to FSx for Windows: FSx File Gateway on premises.

why: Amazon Textract extracts printed and handwritten text from PDF and JPEG documents with a managed API. Amazon Comprehend Medical is a HIPAA-eligible service that detects PHI in text, so combining them in the Lambda code requires no model building and has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Using and maintaining custom Python libraries to detect PHI requires more development and is less accurate.
others.B: Building a PHI detection model in SageMaker adds significant operational and development overhead.
others.D: Rekognition text detection is for short text in images and is not designed for document text extraction like Textract.

tip: Documents to text: Textract; PHI or medical entities in text: Comprehend Medical.

why: S3 Standard-IA provides millisecond access and the same durability as S3 Standard at a lower storage price for rarely accessed data, fitting the always-immediate-access requirement after 30 days. A Lifecycle rule transitions files after 30 days and expires them after 4 years, as policy allows deletion then.

others.A: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide immediate access; retrieval takes minutes to hours.
others.B: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, risking loss of critical data that is hard to reproduce.
others.D: Moving files to Glacier after 4 years keeps paying for storage when the files can simply be deleted.

tip: Infrequent but immediate access with high durability: Standard-IA (or Glacier Instant Retrieval).

why: If processing takes longer than the queue's visibility timeout, the message becomes visible again and another instance receives and processes it, causing duplicate RDS records. Increasing the visibility timeout with ChangeMessageVisibility (or on the queue) ensures the message stays hidden until it is processed and deleted.

others.A: Creating a new queue does not change how long messages stay hidden during processing.
others.B: Permissions do not affect duplicate processing.
others.C: The ReceiveMessage wait time controls long polling, not message visibility during processing.

tip: Duplicate processing from SQS: visibility timeout shorter than processing time.

why: AWS Direct Connect provides a private connection with consistent low latency to the Region. A Site-to-Site VPN over the internet as a backup is inexpensive and provides failover with slower, less consistent performance, which the company accepts, minimizing cost.

others.B: VPN tunnels over the internet do not provide consistent low latency for the primary connection.
others.C: A second Direct Connect connection gives better resiliency but costs significantly more than a VPN backup.
others.D: There is no Direct Connect failover attribute that automatically creates a backup connection.

tip: Cost-effective Direct Connect backup when slower failover is acceptable: Site-to-Site VPN.

why: Spreading the Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs and making the Aurora database Multi-AZ (with an Aurora Replica in another AZ) provides automatic failover with minimal downtime and data loss. RDS Proxy pools connections and further reduces failover times, all with little operational effort.

others.A: A multi-Region design with cross-Region replication adds significant complexity and is beyond what high availability requires.
others.C: A single AZ is not highly available, and hourly snapshots risk up to an hour of data loss.
others.D: Writing through S3 and Lambda across Regions is complex and does not make the database highly available.

tip: HA within a Region: Multi-AZ for compute and database.

why: NLB health checks can use HTTP, but an Application Load Balancer is the natural fit for an HTTP application, with HTTP health checks against the application URL that detect HTTP errors. Configuring the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks then replaces unhealthy instances automatically, with no custom scripts.

others.A: The keyed answer treats NLB HTTP health checks as insufficient; and without Auto Scaling using ELB health checks, unhealthy instances would not be replaced automatically.
others.B: No alarm is defined in this option, and it does not detect HTTP errors.
others.D: Monitoring UnhealthyHostCount alone does not detect or remediate HTTP errors without further automation.

tip: Auto-replace instances failing app checks: ELB HTTP health checks plus ASG ELB health check type.

why: The option text for B is missing in this question bank; the intended answer is to configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR) and restore to a point in time. PITR continuously backs up the table and can restore to any second in the last 35 days, so an RPO of 15 minutes is easily met, and restoring to a new table typically completes within the 1-hour RTO.

others.A: Global tables replicate corruption to all Regions almost immediately, so they do not protect against data corruption.
others.C: Daily exports give an RPO of up to 24 hours, and restoring from Glacier is slow.
others.D: DynamoDB is a managed service and does not use EBS volumes that can be snapshotted.

tip: DynamoDB corruption recovery with fine-grained RPO: point-in-time recovery. Option B text is blank in this bank.

why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint routes traffic from the VPC to S3 in the same Region over the AWS network without NAT gateway processing charges, and gateway endpoints are free. An endpoint policy can restrict access to the specific buckets, reducing data transfer costs.

others.A: API Gateway is not a routing target for S3 traffic and would add per-request charges.
others.B: NAT gateways charge per GB processed, which is the source of the increased cost, and endpoint policies do not apply to NAT gateways.
others.C: Moving the application to a public subnet reduces security and still does not offer the cost and privacy benefits of an endpoint.

tip: Same-Region S3 traffic cost via NAT: use a gateway endpoint.

why: The bastion host is reached from on premises over the internet, so its security group should allow SSH only from the company's external (public) IP range. The application instances in the private subnet should allow SSH only from the bastion host's private IP address, because traffic within the VPC uses private addresses.

others.A: Allowing inbound access only from the application instances would block administrators connecting from on premises.
others.B: Traffic from on premises over the internet arrives from the company's public IP addresses, not internal ranges.
others.E: Traffic from the bastion to private instances within the VPC uses the bastion's private IP, not its public IP.

tip: Bastion SG: allow company public IPs; private instances SG: allow bastion private IP or its SG.

why: The public web tier must accept HTTPS from anywhere, so its security group allows inbound port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. The database tier should allow inbound SQL Server traffic on port 1433 only from the web tier's security group, following least privilege.

others.B: Security groups allow all outbound traffic by default, and outbound rules do not have a source.
others.D: Security groups are stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically; outbound rules to the web tier are unnecessary.
others.E: Opening port 443 on the database tier is unnecessary and violates least privilege.

tip: Security groups are stateful; define inbound rules and reference source security groups.

why: API Gateway with Lambda functions provides an automatically scaling serverless application layer, and SQS queues between services buffer requests so transactions are not dropped when a tier is overloaded. This modernizes the application with the most operational efficiency.

others.B: Vertically scaling EC2 instances does not decouple tiers or prevent drops during unexpected spikes, and keeps server management.
others.C: SNS does not have a queue length to monitor and does not buffer messages for later processing.
others.D: SQS with EC2 Auto Scaling works but still requires managing servers, and scaling only after failures is reactive.

tip: Modernize and decouple with least ops: API Gateway, Lambda, SQS.

why: AWS DataSync transfers file data from on-premises storage to S3 with encryption in transit, integrity validation and automatic retries. Running it over AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection with consistent bandwidth for the daily 10 TB, making this the most reliable and secure transfer.

others.A: DataSync over the public internet is secure but less reliable and consistent than a dedicated connection.
others.C: DMS is for database migration, not for transferring JSON files from a SAN.
others.D: DMS is not designed for file transfers, regardless of the network used.

tip: Recurring file transfer to S3: DataSync; reliability and consistency: Direct Connect.

why: API Gateway provides a fully managed API that can send records directly to a Kinesis data stream. Kinesis Data Firehose reads from the stream, transforms records in flight using Lambda, and delivers them to S3, so every component is managed and the design has the least operational overhead.

others.A: Hosting the API on an EC2 instance adds server management overhead.
others.B: An EC2 instance adds overhead, Glue is not a streaming ingestion endpoint for an API, and source/destination checks are irrelevant.
others.D: AWS Glue is not a direct API Gateway integration target for real-time streaming ingestion.

tip: Managed real-time pipeline: API Gateway to Kinesis Data Streams to Firehose (Lambda transform) to S3.

why: AWS Backup supports DynamoDB with centrally managed backup plans that define schedules, retention periods of years, and lifecycle transitions to cold storage. Setting a 7-year retention policy automates long-term backups with no custom code, making it the most operationally efficient.

others.A: Point-in-time recovery only retains continuous backups for up to 35 days.
others.C: Manual on-demand backups from the console do not scale operationally, and DynamoDB backups are not directly stored in your own S3 bucket.
others.D: A custom Lambda backup process requires writing and maintaining code.

tip: Long-term scheduled backups with retention: AWS Backup.

why: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode charges per request and instantly accommodates sudden, unpredictable traffic spikes without capacity planning. When the table is idle in the mornings, you pay nothing for throughput, making it cost-optimized for this pattern.

others.B: A global secondary index adds query flexibility, not cost optimization or spike handling.
others.C: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling reacts over minutes and may throttle on very fast spikes, and you pay for minimum provisioned capacity while idle.
others.D: Global tables replicate across Regions, increasing cost without addressing unpredictable traffic.

tip: Unpredictable or spiky DynamoDB traffic: on-demand mode.

why: Modifying the AMI's launchPermission to share it with only the MSP Partner's account limits exposure to that account. Because the snapshots are encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, the key policy must also allow the partner account to use the key, making this the most secure sharing method.

others.A: Making the AMI and snapshots public exposes them to everyone and is not secure; encrypted AMIs cannot be shared publicly anyway.
others.C: The partner needs permissions on the source key to use the encrypted snapshots; a key policy cannot trust another KMS key.
others.D: Exporting the AMI to S3 adds unnecessary steps and is not the standard secure sharing method.

tip: Share encrypted AMI: share with the account and grant access to the customer managed KMS key.

why: An SQS queue durably stores job items and decouples producers from processors. An Auto Scaling group using a launch template scales stateless processor instances based on the number of messages in the queue, directly matching nodes to the number of jobs.

others.A: SNS does not durably store jobs for workers to pull, and CPU usage does not reflect job backlog.
others.B: Network usage is not a good proxy for job count, and launch configurations are deprecated in favor of launch templates.
others.D: SNS pushes messages and does not hold a backlog, so scaling on published messages does not reflect pending work.

tip: Scale workers on queue depth (backlog per instance).

why: ACM emits daily 'ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration' events to EventBridge starting before expiration (the threshold is configurable). An EventBridge rule can match these events, filter for 30 days, and invoke a Lambda function that sends a custom alert through SNS.

others.A: ACM has no feature to add custom rules that publish messages on a schedule.
others.B: An AWS Config rule (acm-certificate-expiration-check) is also viable, but the option requires additional custom alert wiring and is not the keyed approach.
others.C: Trusted Advisor checks for expiring certificates are not designed for a precise 30-day custom alert workflow via CloudWatch metrics.

tip: ACM expiration events go to EventBridge; imported certificates are not auto-renewed.

why: Amazon CloudFront can use a custom origin, including on-premises servers, and serves content through edge locations in Europe, caching static assets and accelerating dynamic requests over the AWS backbone. It can be set up within days while the backend stays in the United States.

others.A: Migrating to an EC2 instance in us-east-1 does not reduce latency for European users and takes time.
others.B: A dynamic website cannot be hosted on S3, and the backend must remain in the United States.
others.D: Geoproximity routing to the same on-premises servers does not reduce latency for European users.

tip: Speed up global access to an existing origin quickly: CloudFront with custom origin.

why: Production instances run 24/7 with steady usage, so Reserved Instances (or Savings Plans) give the largest discount. Development and test instances run only part of each day and will be stopped by automation, so On-Demand pricing avoids paying for unused reserved hours.

others.A: Spot Instances can be interrupted, which is unacceptable for production, and RIs for part-time instances waste money.
others.C: Spot blocks are no longer offered and are unsuitable for 24/7 production; RIs for part-time instances are wasteful.
others.D: On-Demand for 24/7 production is more expensive than RIs, and Spot blocks are discontinued.

tip: Steady 24/7: Reserved Instances or Savings Plans; intermittent: On-Demand; interruptible: Spot.

why: S3 Object Lock provides write-once-read-many (WORM) protection so object versions cannot be overwritten or deleted during the retention period, and it requires S3 Versioning to be enabled. This directly meets the regulatory requirement that stored documents cannot be modified or deleted.

others.B: Lifecycle archiving does not prevent modification or deletion.
others.C: ACLs can be changed by privileged users and read-only access would also block uploads.
others.D: Mounting EFS read-only on clients does not prevent deletion by other clients and is not a compliance control.

tip: WORM compliance in S3: Object Lock (requires Versioning).

why: AWS Secrets Manager stores database credentials securely and can rotate them automatically on a schedule for Amazon RDS MySQL. Web servers with IAM permissions retrieve current credentials at runtime, meeting the frequent rotation requirement securely.

others.B: Systems Manager OpsCenter is for managing operational issues (OpsItems), not storing credentials.
others.C: Storing credentials in S3 offers no automatic rotation.
others.D: KMS-encrypted local files require manual distribution and rotation across web servers.

tip: Frequent credential rotation: Secrets Manager.

why: Writing customer data to an SQS FIFO queue durably stores it even while the database is unavailable during upgrades. A separate Lambda function polls the queue and writes the data to Aurora once the database is available, with failed messages retried, so no data is lost.

others.A: RDS Proxy pools connections and speeds failover but cannot accept writes while the database is down for an upgrade.
others.B: Lambda functions time out after at most 15 minutes, and in-code retries may still lose data during longer upgrades.
others.C: Lambda local storage (/tmp) is ephemeral and not shared across invocations or functions.

tip: Database temporarily unavailable: buffer writes in SQS.

why: With S3 Requester Pays enabled, the requester (the marketing firm) pays the request and data transfer costs for downloading data from the bucket. The company pays only for storage, keeping its data transfer costs as low as possible.

others.B: Cross-Region Replication incurs inter-Region data transfer charges that the company pays.
others.C: Cross-account access alone still leaves the bucket owner paying for data transfer out.
others.D: Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage cost, and syncing to another bucket still incurs transfer costs for the company.

tip: Shift download costs to consumers: S3 Requester Pays.

why: S3 Versioning preserves every object version so deleted documents can be recovered, and MFA Delete requires an MFA code from the bucket owner (root) to permanently delete versions or disable versioning. Together they protect the audit documents against accidental deletion.

others.B: MFA on sign-in protects credentials but does not stop an authenticated user from accidentally deleting objects.
others.C: Lifecycle policies apply to buckets, not IAM users, and cannot deny API actions.
others.D: Restricting KMS key access would block the audit team from reading documents and does not prevent deletion.

tip: Accidental deletion protection: Versioning plus MFA Delete.

why: An RDS read replica offloads the script's read-only queries from the primary DB instance, so the development team's workload is no longer impacted. Creating a replica and pointing the script at its endpoint is quick with the least operational overhead.

others.A: The Multi-AZ standby (in the classic instance deployment) cannot serve reads, so it does not offload the script.
others.C: Manual daily exports add operational effort and do not provide reports during business hours.
others.D: ElastiCache requires application changes and cache management, and random counting queries may not benefit from caching.

tip: Offload read-heavy reporting from the primary: read replica.

why: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint lets EC2 instances reach the S3 API through the AWS private network via a route table entry, so no traffic traverses the internet. It requires no NAT or internet gateway and is free.

others.B: S3 buckets are Regional services and cannot be placed in a subnet.
others.C: Placing the bucket in the same Region does not by itself keep traffic off the internet path.
others.D: A NAT gateway sends traffic to S3 public endpoints via the internet gateway, and it must be in a public subnet.

tip: No internet path to S3: gateway endpoint.

why: A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 keeps traffic between the application tier and the bucket on the AWS network. The option text for C is missing in this bank; the intended choice is a bucket policy that restricts access to the application tier, for example by allowing only requests through the VPC endpoint (aws:SourceVpce) or from the application's IAM role.

others.B: Making objects public exposes sensitive user information to everyone.
others.D: Copying long-term IAM user credentials to instances is insecure; use an IAM role instead.
others.E: A NAT instance routes traffic over the internet and adds management overhead.

tip: Secure S3 from a VPC: gateway endpoint plus bucket policy conditioned on the endpoint or role. Option C text is blank in this bank.

why: Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas across AZs offloads heavy read activity and provides high availability. Aurora database cloning uses a copy-on-write protocol to create a staging copy in minutes without a full export, so production latency is unaffected and developers can use staging immediately.

others.A: mysqldump full exports still load the production database and take time, delaying staging.
others.C: The RDS Multi-AZ standby cannot be accessed or used as a staging database.
others.D: mysqldump backup and restore still causes latency and delays for staging.

tip: Fast copy of an Aurora database for test or staging: Aurora cloning.

why: S3 event notifications to SQS durably capture each upload, and a Lambda function processes messages as soon as they arrive and scales with demand down to zero. Storing the resulting JSON in DynamoDB is fully managed, giving the least operational overhead.

others.A: An EMR cluster is heavy for simple per-file processing and incurs costs even on idle days, and Aurora adds management.
others.B: Option B text is missing in this question bank, so it cannot be evaluated.
others.D: Adding EventBridge and Kinesis Data Streams with shards and an Aurora cluster adds unnecessary components and overhead.

tip: Event-driven per-file processing: S3 to SQS to Lambda. Option B text is blank in this bank.

why: RDS read replicas separate read traffic from writes by serving reads from replica endpoints, which is a quick change. Replicas should have the same compute and storage as the source so they can keep up with replication and the read load.

others.A: In a Multi-AZ instance deployment, reads are already served from the primary, so it does not separate traffic.
others.B: The Multi-AZ standby in a classic deployment cannot serve read traffic.
others.C: Undersized replicas can suffer replication lag and poor read performance.

tip: Separate reads from writes in RDS: read replicas sized like the source.

why: The policy image is not included in this bank. In the original question, the policy allows ec2:TerminateInstances when the source IP condition is 10.100.100.0/24 and denies EC2 actions outside us-east-1. A user with source IP 10.100.100.254 is within the allowed CIDR, so the user can terminate instances in us-east-1.

others.A: The policy denies actions in Regions other than us-east-1, so terminating elsewhere is not allowed.
others.B: The IP condition applies to the caller's source IP (aws:SourceIp), not the instance's IP address.
others.D: 10.100.100.254 is within the allowed source CIDR, so termination is permitted, not denied.

tip: aws:SourceIp evaluates the requester's IP, not the resource's. Policy image is missing in this bank.

why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed native SMB file shares that integrate with Microsoft Active Directory for access control. Multi-AZ deployments provide high availability, and it is the AWS-recommended storage for SharePoint workloads.

others.A: Amazon EFS uses NFS and does not support Windows SMB or Active Directory authentication.
others.B: Storage Gateway file gateways are for hybrid access to S3 and are not a highly available multi-AZ file share for SharePoint.
others.C: S3 is object storage and cannot be natively mounted as a Windows volume.

tip: Windows shared storage with AD: FSx for Windows File Server.

why: If the SQS visibility timeout is shorter than the time Lambda takes to process a batch, messages reappear and are processed again, causing duplicate emails. AWS recommends setting the visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout plus the batching window, which fixes the issue with a simple configuration change.

others.A: Long polling reduces empty responses but does not stop messages from becoming visible again during processing.
others.B: S3 event notifications cannot target SQS FIFO queues, and migrating queues adds overhead.
others.D: Deleting messages before processing risks losing messages if processing fails.

tip: Duplicate Lambda invocations from SQS: increase visibility timeout beyond function timeout.

why: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed, high-performance file system that is accessed with the Lustre client. On-premises Lustre clients can mount it over Direct Connect or VPN, meeting the shared storage and fully managed requirements.

others.A: Storage Gateway file gateways support NFS and SMB, not the Lustre protocol.
others.B: A self-managed Windows file share is not fully managed and does not support Lustre clients.
others.C: Amazon EFS cannot be configured to support the Lustre protocol.

tip: Lustre or HPC file system needs: FSx for Lustre.

why: AWS KMS customer managed keys provide highly secure, managed encryption and decryption via fast API calls, and the EC2 role can be granted permissions to use the key. Storing the encrypted data in Amazon S3 provides highly available, durable storage across multiple AZs with no infrastructure to manage.

others.A: Manually updating secrets adds overhead, and Secrets Manager is not meant for near-real-time encryption of arbitrary data.
others.B: A custom Lambda encryption function adds development overhead, and functions are not stored in S3 to run.
others.D: EBS volumes reside in a single AZ and are less highly available than S3.

tip: Managed encryption: KMS; highly available storage: S3 (multi-AZ) over EBS (single AZ).

why: NAT gateways placed in each AZ's public subnet allow instances in private subnets to initiate outbound IPv4 internet connections. A private route table per AZ that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway in the same AZ avoids cross-AZ dependency, preserving high availability.

others.B: NAT instances must be in public subnets and require management; placing them in private subnets does not work.
others.C: A VPC can have only one internet gateway, and private subnets by definition do not route to it.
others.D: Egress-only internet gateways support only IPv6 traffic, not IPv4.

tip: IPv4 outbound for private subnets: NAT gateway per AZ; IPv6: egress-only internet gateway.

why: AWS DataSync automates and accelerates transfers from on-premises NFS storage to Amazon EFS. Installing a DataSync agent in the data center and creating a source location for the on-premises server's file system lets DataSync copy the 200 GB directly to EFS.

others.A: EFS is accessible from all AZs in the Region, and AZ placement does not automate the transfer.
others.C: An extra EBS volume is unnecessary because the data must reside on EFS.
others.D: Manual copy commands are not automated.

tip: Automated on-prem NFS/SMB to EFS, FSx or S3: DataSync with an agent.

why: AWS Glue job bookmarks track state from previous runs so the job processes only new data added to the S3 source. Enabling bookmarks prevents reprocessing old data on each daily run.

others.B: Deleting source data after processing is destructive and unnecessary.
others.C: Reducing workers only slows the job and still reprocesses all data.
others.D: FindMatches is an ML transform for deduplicating or matching records, not for incremental processing.

tip: Glue incremental processing: job bookmarks.

why: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced detection and automatic mitigation of large-scale DDoS attacks with 24/7 Shield Response Team support. Serving both static and dynamic content through Amazon CloudFront absorbs attack traffic across the global edge network, protecting the origin and keeping the site available.

others.B: GuardDuty detects threats but does not automatically block DDoS traffic.
others.D: Network ACLs have a limited number of rules and cannot handle thousands of attacker IPs.
others.E: Spot Instances can be interrupted, risking downtime, and scaling does not mitigate DDoS.

tip: DDoS protection: CloudFront (edge absorption) plus Shield Advanced, optionally with AWS WAF.

why: For EventBridge to invoke a Lambda function, the function's resource-based policy must grant lambda:InvokeFunction to the events.amazonaws.com service principal. Limiting the action to InvokeFunction (and optionally the rule ARN as source) follows least privilege.

others.A: Execution roles define what the function can do, not who can invoke it, and a wildcard principal is not least privilege.
others.B: Execution roles do not control invocation, and lambda.amazonaws.com is not the invoking service.
others.C: lambda:* grants far more permissions than needed.

tip: Who can invoke Lambda: resource-based policy; what Lambda can access: execution role.

why: SSE-KMS encrypts data at rest with KMS keys, and every key use is logged in AWS CloudTrail for auditing. Enabling automatic key rotation on a customer managed key rotates the key material every year by default, making it the most operationally efficient option.

others.A: SSE-C requires the customer to manage and rotate keys, and key usage is not logged by KMS.
others.B: SSE-S3 does not provide auditable key usage logs or customer control over rotation.
others.C: Manual rotation requires additional operational effort compared with automatic rotation.

tip: Auditable key usage plus yearly rotation: SSE-KMS with automatic rotation.

why: Amazon API Gateway provides the REST API for location updates, and Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics processes the streaming location data in real time, feeding results into the existing analytics platform. This multi-tier design handles streaming location data during peak hours.

others.A: Athena with S3 is for ad hoc querying and does not provide a REST API for real-time location data.
others.B: API Gateway with Lambda can provide the API, but by itself it offers no storage or streaming analytics for the location data.
others.C: QuickSight with Redshift is a visualization and warehouse solution, not a REST-accessible tier for location data.

tip: Real-time streaming analytics behind an API: API Gateway plus Kinesis.

why: A Lambda function invoked when the database is updated (for example, from an Aurora or RDS trigger or application logic) can send the sold-listing data to an SQS queue for the target systems to consume. This decouples the website from downstream systems.

others.B: FIFO queues add throughput limits and ordering that are not required here.
others.C: SQS cannot fan out to multiple SNS topics; fan-out is SNS to SQS.
others.D: RDS event notifications report instance-level events such as failovers and backups, not data changes like a listing being sold.

tip: RDS event notifications are operational events, not row-level data changes.

why: S3 Object Lock legal holds prevent an object version from being overwritten or deleted with no expiration date, which matches 'unchangeable for a nonspecific amount of time'. Object Lock requires versioning, and only users granted s3:PutObjectLegalHold can remove the hold and then delete objects, limiting deletion to specific users.

others.A: S3 Glacier vault lock applies to archives in vaults, not S3 objects, and locked policies cannot be changed to allow specific users.
others.B: A fixed 100-year retention period is not a nonspecific duration, and governance mode bypass is managed with a different permission.
others.C: CloudTrail notifications with restores are reactive and do not prevent changes.
